key_insight: A 3D U-Net predicts full 36-component strain localization tensor fields by scaling network width and depth, while conventional channel-doubling is suboptimal for this task.
engineering_relevance: The surrogate could accelerate repeated mechanical-field calculations in concrete homogenization and coupled multiscale simulations.
method: Train on voxelized concrete mesostructures up to 256³ using localization tensors from an FFT-based linear elastic solver.
Optimize U-Net architecture to derive scaling rules and accuracy–speed trade-offs.
Use Maximum Mean Discrepancy on internal feature maps to flag out-of-distribution microstructures without reference solves.
evidence_signal: The final model reports 1.118% mean absolute error on both validation and held-out test sets, approximately 8.7× inference speedup over the FFT solver on an Nvidia H100 GPU, and transfer across aggregate volume fractions.
watch_item: Generalization depends on morphological diversity in training; out-of-distribution detection is a warning mechanism, not an accuracy guarantee.
paper_title: Neural network scaling and generalization for 3D strain fields in heterogeneous materials
